name: SAUND
full_name: Study of Acoustic Ultra-high-energy Neutrino Detection
summary: A historical feasibility experiment used US Navy hydrophones in the Bahamas to search for bipolar acoustic pulses from ultra-high-energy neutrino interactions in a very large volume of sea water.
detection_principle: A particle cascade deposits energy rapidly and heats a narrow volume of water, producing a short bipolar pressure pulse. Several hydrophone coincidences and reconstructed source positions are used to distinguish this signal from marine and instrumental backgrounds.
technologies: Thermo-acoustic particle detection with hydrophones or piezoelectric sensors

key_parameters.name: SAUND-II array
key_parameters.value: Approximately 20 × 50 km; hydrophones at 1,340–1,880 m depth

results.summary: Two events survived the radiation-pattern selection. Their nature could not be established with the small sample and incompletely known impulsive backgrounds; conservative upper limits counted them as possible signal, without claiming an acoustic-neutrino discovery.

science_scope: Published limits are not neutrino detections. Instrument or exposure parameters refer to the explicitly named campaign; research prototypes and future designs are distinguished.
